title: Add the combined engine and client install mode
summary: The Forgel Code installer, run with no extra flags, installs the engine alongside the client, so the documented one-command install yields a working pair. It is idempotent by comparing the installed engine against the version the configured engine source provides: no engine installs it, an installed engine at or above the available one is kept untouched, a strictly newer available engine replaces it, and the finished result always satisfies the declared minimum, failing with an actionable message when it cannot. The default engine source is a documented configuration, and the run reports which engine version is installed.
requirements: The default client installation also ensures a supported engine is in place in the same run.
The installation learns which engine version the configured engine source offers without changing anything on the machine.
When no engine is present, the installation obtains the offered engine version.
When an engine is present and the offered version is not strictly newer, the installation keeps the present engine and changes nothing about the engine installation.
When the offered version is strictly newer than the present engine, the installation replaces the present engine with that newer one.
The installation never installs an engine older than, or equal to, the one already present.
The finished state always satisfies the client's declared minimum supported engine version; when it cannot, the installation ends as a failure instead of reporting the pair as installed.
A failed engine outcome reports the required minimum version, the version that was found or offered, and a concrete action the user can take, and is clearly distinguishable from a successful run.
A successful installation states the engine version in place and how it was obtained: installed, kept or replaced.

Engine versions are ordered numerically component by component, tolerating one leading version prefix and trailing zero components; a version that cannot be ordered never counts as satisfying the minimum.
The documented client-only installation installs the client and neither queries nor changes any engine.
Removing the client installs nothing and leaves any engine in place.
The documented option that keeps the user's startup configuration unchanged does not disable the engine part of the installation.
The engine source the installation resolves against is documented configuration with a stated default and a documented way to point it elsewhere.
Repeating the default installation changes nothing about an engine that needs no change, and leaves exactly one client installation and one startup entry.

The user documentation presents the default installation as the way to obtain a working client-and-engine pair, documents the client-only installation and the engine source configuration, and no longer instructs the user to supply an engine separately.
The project's automated checks contain no check that reads documentation text, and no automated check of documentation text is added in its place.
The correctness of the installation instructions is accepted or returned solely by review of their text.
Every other automated check stays in place and unchanged, and the installer and client behavior outside the combined installation is unchanged.
acceptance: Starting the default installation on a machine with no engine ends successfully, leaves a usable client, leaves an engine at or above the declared minimum, and reports that version and that it was installed.

Starting the default installation with an engine already present at exactly the offered version ends successfully, leaves the engine installation unchanged, and reports the engine as kept with its version.
Starting the default installation with an engine present below the offered version ends successfully, leaves the strictly newer offered engine in place, and reports it as replaced.

Starting the default installation with an engine present above the offered version and at or above the declared minimum ends successfully, leaves the engine installation unchanged, and reports the engine as kept.

When the offered version is below the declared minimum and no suitable engine is present, the installation ends as a failure whose message names the required minimum, the version found or offered, and the action the user can take.
When obtaining the engine fails, the installation ends as a failure with a message naming what went wrong and the next action, and never reports the pair as installed.
Choosing the documented client-only installation installs the client, performs no engine version query, and leaves an engine present beforehand unchanged.
Running the default installation twice in a row leaves exactly one client installation and one startup entry, and the second run does not change the engine the first run left.
Versions differing only by a leading version prefix or by trailing zero components are treated as the same version, and a version that cannot be ordered never satisfies the minimum.
Removing a client installed with an engine leaves the engine in place and leaves no client artifacts behind.

The documentation presents the default installation as producing a working client alongside a supported engine, states that the engine version in place and how it was obtained are reported, and describes what a successful installation reports.

The documentation states that an absent engine is obtained, that a present engine is kept when the offered version is not strictly newer, that a strictly newer offered engine replaces it, and that the finished state always satisfies the declared minimum or the installation fails with an actionable message naming the minimum and the version found or offered.

The documentation documents the client-only installation, the engine source with its default and how to point it elsewhere, and the option that keeps the user's startup configuration unchanged; it no longer instructs the user to supply an engine separately for the default installation.
The automated checks contain no check that reads documentation text, and no automated check of documentation text replaces the removed one.
All other automated checks run unchanged and pass, and installer and client behavior outside the combined installation is unchanged.
The installation instructions are accepted or returned solely by review of their text; a passing or failing verdict on their wording comes from a person reading them, never from an automated check.
constraints: No automated check reads documentation text; the installation instructions are verified by review of their text only, and no automated documentation check is added in place of the removed one.
The removed documentation check is deleted in full, including the supporting data that reproduces the documentation text.
No other automated check is removed, weakened or skipped, and installer and client behavior outside the combined installation is unchanged.
The combined installation is idempotent, never installs an engine older than or equal to the one present, and always ends at or above the declared minimum or as a failure.
All project artifacts are written in English, regardless of chat language.
plan_goal: Make Forgel and Forgel Code install and run as one working pair: give the engine `forgel` its own installer, add a mode of the Forgel Code installer that installs both binaries together (offered by default in the README, idempotent — when the engine is already present it compares versions and installs only a strictly newer one), and introduce a declared minimum supported engine version for Forgel Code, checked at startup, so a missing or too-old engine produces a clear actionable message instead of `engine forgel: executable not found: forgel`.

result.summary: Implemented the combined engine and client installation for Forgel Code. install.sh now performs the client installation and, in the same default run, settles the engine: it reads the version the configured engine source offers through the engine's own installer (installing nothing) and the version of an engine already in place, then obtains an absent engine, keeps a present engine when the offered version is not strictly newer, and replaces a present engine only with a strictly newer offered version. Versions are ordered numerically component by component with one leading prefix and trailing zeros tolerated; an unorderable version never satisfies the minimum. The client's declared minimum engine version (MIN_ENGINE_VERSION in forgel_code/__init__.py) is the single source, and the run fails with a message naming the required minimum, the version found or offered and the user's next action whenever the end state cannot satisfy it. Successful runs report the engine version and whether it was installed, kept or replaced. --client-only installs the client without querying or touching any engine, FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH still performs the engine part, --uninstall installs nothing and leaves the engine in place, and repeating the default run changes no engine that needs no change and leaves one client installation and one startup entry. FORGEL_ENGINE_SOURCE and FORGEL_ENGINE_INSTALLER are documented configuration with defaults. README documents the combined default installation, the decision table, the success and failure reports, the client-only route, the engine source configuration and the startup-configuration opt-out, and no longer tells the user to supply an engine separately for the default installation. The automated documentation check (tests/test_readme_install.py and ReadmeTest in tests/test_cli.py, including the pinned URL data) is deleted in full and nothing replaces it. Tests cover the combined installation against a deterministic stand-in of the engine's installer (tests/stub_engine_install.py): absent, kept, replaced, failure, client-only, repeated install and removal scenarios. The full suite passes: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests (367 tests, OK).
assumptions: A version that cannot be ordered is handled as 'not present' for the purpose of the decision, so a supported offered version replaces such an engine and an unorderable offered version fails the run.
The engine's own installer is the dependency that answers the offered version and performs installation; the client decides and delegates but never reimplements it.
The installed client's minimum engine version is declared once in forgel_code/__init__.py and read from there by the installer, so the two cannot drift.
The README installation instructions are verified only by review; no automated check of documentation text exists and none was added.
The CHANGELOG [Unreleased] section records the combined installation and the removal of the automated documentation check.

review.summary: The attributed change implements the combined install: install.sh gains an engine phase that learns the offered version from the configured source without changing anything, reads the present engine version, then keeps, replaces or obtains the engine, enforces the client's declared minimum (`MIN_ENGINE_VERSION` in `forgel_code/__init__.py`), and reports `Engine: forgel <version> <installed|kept|replaced>` or fails with the minimum, the found/offered version and an action. A deterministic stand-in (`tests/stub_engine_install.py`) mirrors the recorded engine-installer contract and the new `tests/test_install_engine.py` exercises obtain/keep/replace/failure/client-only/uninstall/repeat cases through the real installer. The documentation check (`tests/test_readme_install.py` and the `ReadmeTest` in `tests/test_cli.py`) is deleted together with its supporting data and replaced by nothing, and the README/CHANGELOG are updated to describe the combined installation, the engine source, the client-only route, the no-profile-edit option and the leave-engine-on-uninstall behaviour. QA reports all repository and environment checks passing, the worktree is clean, and the removed tests carry justified `removed` reasons consistent with the mandated removal of documentation-reading checks. No unrelated, temporary or generated file is part of the attributed change, and I found no logical or security defect in the reviewed parts.

requirements.requirement: Default installation also ensures a supported engine in the same run (FR-1, AC-1)
requirements.note: install.sh performs the engine phase by default; `EngineObtainedTest.test_absent_engine_is_installed_and_reported` shows the client plus an installed engine reported as `Engine: forgel 0.2.0 installed`.

requirements.requirement: The offered version is learned without changing the machine (FR-2)
requirements.note: The engine installer is queried with `--available-version` through the stub contract, which installs nothing; `install_calls()` remains empty in the keep cases.

requirements.requirement: Absent engine is obtained; a present engine at or above the offered version is kept unchanged (FR-3, FR-4, AC-2, AC-4)
requirements.note: `EngineObtainedTest` and `EngineKeptTest` assert an unchanged engine version and no install call for equal and higher present versions.

requirements.requirement: A strictly newer offered engine replaces the present one; an engine older than or equal to the present one is never installed (FR-5, FR-6, AC-3)
requirements.note: `EngineReplacedTest` covers replacement; keep cases assert `install_calls() == []`, so no equal or older version is installed.

requirements.requirement: The finished state satisfies the declared minimum or the run fails (FR-7, AC-5, AC-6)
requirements.note: Minimum is declared once in `forgel_code/__init__.py`, and the tests use `_declared_minimum()`; failure message contents are asserted by the failure scenarios covered by the passing repository checks.

requirements.requirement: A failed engine outcome reports the minimum, the found or offered version and an action, and is distinguishable from success (FR-8)
requirements.note: The installer tracks ENGINE_MINIMUM/ENGINE_PRESENT/ENGINE_AVAILABLE for the failure report and exits non-zero; the README documents that the failure names the minimum, version and next action.

requirements.requirement: A successful installation states the engine version in place and how it was obtained (FR-9, AC-11)
requirements.note: Asserted by the `Engine: forgel <version> installed|kept|replaced` lines in the engine tests and described in the README.

requirements.requirement: Version ordering tolerates one leading prefix and trailing zeros; an unorderable version never satisfies the minimum (FR-10, AC-9)
requirements.note: `test_a_prefix_or_trailing_zeros_do_not_make_a_newer_version` keeps `v0.1.0.0` against offered `0.1`; the installer's comparison is component-wise and the README states the ordering rule.

requirements.requirement: The client-only installation installs the client and neither queries nor changes any engine (FR-11, AC-7)
requirements.note: `--client-only` short-circuits the engine phase before any query; the README documents that route and the installer advertises the flag.

requirements.requirement: Removing the client installs nothing and leaves any engine in place (FR-12, AC-10)
requirements.note: The uninstall path removes the prefix, launcher and PATH block only; the README states it leaves any engine in place.

requirements.requirement: The startup-configuration opt-out does not disable the engine part (FR-13)
requirements.note: `FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH` only skips profile editing and the fresh-shell check; the README states the engine part still happens.

requirements.requirement: The engine source is documented configuration with a stated default and a way to point it elsewhere (FR-14, AC-13)
requirements.note: README documents `FORGEL_ENGINE_SOURCE` (default `https://github.com/forgel-dev/forgel`) and `FORGEL_ENGINE_INSTALLER`, with an example overriding the source; both are read by install.sh.

requirements.requirement: Repeating the default installation changes nothing that needs no change and leaves one client installation and one startup entry (FR-15, AC-8)
requirements.note: The existing re-run guarantees (one marked block, replaced prefix) are unchanged and the engine keep case issues no install call on the second run.

requirements.requirement: README/CHANGELOG present the default installation as the way to obtain a working pair, document client-only and the engine source, and no longer instruct a separate engine for the default (FR-16, AC-11, AC-12, AC-13)
requirements.note: The README adds 'The engine', 'Engine source' and 'Client only' sections describing the decision table, the failure report, the success report, the variables and the defaults; the prerequisites line no longer asks for the engine on PATH, and the CHANGELOG records the change.

requirements.requirement: No automated check reads documentation text and none replaces it (FR-17, AC-14)
requirements.note: `tests/test_readme_install.py` is deleted in full with its data, `tests/test_cli.py` `ReadmeTest` is removed; no new documentation-reading check is added and no file reads README.md text.

requirements.requirement: Installation instructions are accepted or returned solely by reading their text (FR-18, AC-16)
requirements.note: With the documentation checks gone, no automated verdict over README wording exists; this review judged the wording directly.

requirements.requirement: All other automated checks stay in place and unchanged; installer and client behaviour outside the combined installation is unchanged (FR-19, AC-15)
requirements.note: Remaining tests (packaging, CLI, redaction, interactive, installer) are untouched by the diff; the attributed changes to install.sh only add the engine phase and its reporting.

requirements.requirement: No unrelated, temporary or generated file committed
requirements.note: The attributed files are the installer, the version module, the README, the CHANGELOG, the engine stub and the engine/install/CLI tests; no debug or generated artifacts appear.

requirements.requirement: No weakened or unjustifiably deleted test
requirements.note: The only deletions are the documentation-reading check and its CLI counterpart, both justified as `removed` by the mandated elimination of checks over documentation text (D-106), with no replacement check over documentation.
